statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96238 is a .NET SDK security feature bypass in the template engine (Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge): dotnet new install can acquire a template package from a feed that NuGet Package Source Mapping does not permit, bypassing the configured feed trust boundary. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms and the .NET SDK 10.0.1xx feature band as affected from 10.0.100 through 10.0.112 and fixed in 10.0.113, shipped with .NET 10.0.13 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/486, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56614, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix enables package source mapping in the template engine's NuGet installer (dotnet/dotnet commit 255ecb47edb275f6e384853465ab214b916e075f on release/10.0.1xx; the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.113 source tag, from which the 10.0.13 runtime and SDK 10.0.113 are built, contains it and v10.0.112 does not: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/255ecb47edb275f6e384853465ab214b916e075f). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge.dll ships in every build, in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap (the SDK itself and its bundled dotnet-watch tool) and in the Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and its version is that of each build's SDK: SDK 10.0.102 to 10.0.110 in 10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.10-r0 and SDK 10.0.113 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on; no older SDK copy is present in a later build. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build whose SDK is 10.0.113 or later.

CVE-2026-96238 is a .NET SDK security feature bypass issue in the template engine (Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge): dotnet new install can fetch a template package from a feed that NuGet Package Source Mapping does not allow for it, bypassing the configured feed trust boundary. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected and, for the 8.0.1xx feature band, .NET SDK 8.0.100 through 8.0.131 as affected and 8.0.132 as fixed; .NET 8.0.32 ships with SDK 8.0.132 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/486, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56614, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build holds a .NET SDK in dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap whose version is 8.0.1NN in build 8.0.NN-r0 (8.0.123 in 8.0.23-r0 through 8.0.131 in 8.0.31-r0, then 8.0.132, 8.0.133 and 8.0.134), and dotnet8-runtime-artifacts holds that SDK's own NuGet packages, among them Microsoft.DotNet.Cli and Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge, at the same SDK version, except that the Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge package in 8.0.25-r0 is 8.0.124. In the x86_64 dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap package, the SDK's Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge.dll and command-line assembly dotnet.dll report product version 8.0.131 in 8.0.31-r0 and 8.0.132 in 8.0.32-r0. So 8.0.23-r0 to 8.0.31-r0 carry affected SDKs, and the range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build whose SDK carries the fix.
